extraction.name: Microsoft Common Objects in COntext (MS COCO)
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset designed for object recognition and scene understanding, featuring images of complex everyday scenes. It contains 2.5 million labeled instances across 91 common object categories in 328,000 images, with objects labeled using per-instance segmentations.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Candidate images were collected from Flickr by searching for pairs of object categories or object and scene categories. These candidates were then filtered using an Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) task to remove invalid or iconic images, followed by category labeling and instance spotting.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from Flickr associated with text captions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation process involved multiple stages: an initial filtering task to remove invalid or iconic images, a category labeling task where workers dragged and dropped icons onto object instances, and an instance spotting task where workers clicked on all instances of a specific category.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The 2014 release omits 11 categories due to labeling difficulties, ambiguity, confusion, or extreme instance counts. Additionally, for images with more than ten instances of a category, instances are not individually identified but rather grouped together.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training, validation, and testing of object detection and recognition models. Annotations are provided for train and validation splits, while test evaluation is managed through an automatic evaluation server.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released in versions, starting with a 2014 release limited to 80 categories, followed by a planned cumulative 2015 release that increases the number of images and may include segmentations for previously omitted categories.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An explicit filtering stage was used to remove iconic images when single category searches were necessary.

description.evidence: We present a new dataset with the goal of advancing the state-of-the-art in object recognition by placing the question of object recognition in the context of the broader question of scene understanding. This is achieved by gathering images of complex everyday scenes containing common objects in their natural context. Objects are labeled using per-instance segmentations... rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We did not collect segmentations for the following 11 categories: hat, shoe, eyeglasses (too many instances), mirror, window, door, street sign (ambiguous and difﬁcult to label), plate, desk (due to confusion with bowl and dining table, respectively) and blender, hair brush (too few instances).
